verdict.text: The stray-line check does what the plan asks.
A non-blank line under What changed that is not a `- ` bullet, and is not indented after one, now sends the notes back to the draft with a warning naming stray-line.
The draft's own lines, such as "None.", are exempt.
The tests check the behaviour itself, and the gates are green.
One wrapping nit in the ADR is left.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree myself: lint, format, tests, integration, eval-row r1 and eval-row r2 all pass; stamp green 81dab927a4613846f256fcf1417a0852c52934024770810eb4071c9184234b7a.
Read the full diff (uncommitted in the worktree) and all of scripts/hermes_release_notes.py.

r1: the three parametrized cases (intro, after-a-bullet, between-bullets) assert stdout is the draft byte for byte, that exactly one ::warning:: names "the stray-line check", and that --before is removed.
Without `_stray`, the after-a-bullet and between-bullets lines are joined onto a bullet that has a reference, and the intro is skipped by `_bullets`, so all three would be kept.
The tests would therefore fail on the old code.
r2: the indented-continuation test asserts the wrapped rewrite comes out unchanged with no warning.
The None test builds a draft whose What changed holds "None." (the shape scripts/release_notes.py:212 emits) and would fail without the `known` exemption.
The 19 earlier tests still pass.
Tried edge cases by hand with `check()`.
An indented line before the first bullet is stray.
An indented paragraph after a blank line under a bullet is kept: it is joined onto a bullet that carries a reference, which matches the plan's "indented under one".
A tab-indented nested bullet is kept.
A line with a reference that is not in the draft still hits ref-added first, so it falls back either way.
A draft with no What changed gives `_stray` an empty section, so nothing crashes.
The draft's non-bullet lines come only from scripts/release_notes.py ("None."), not from commit subjects, which always become `- ` bullets.
So the exemption cannot be used to let a crafted line through.
Consistency: the module docstring and ADR 0035 both describe the check correctly and say where it runs in the order.
.okf/summary.md is only re-acked.
